info.title: TgPay Crypto Merchant API
info.summary: Merchant payments API of the TgPay Crypto wallet (@tgpaycryptobot).
info.description:
The Merchant API of TgPay Crypto (@tgpaycryptobot): create
invoices, refund them, send payouts and checks, withdraw the app
balance on-chain, exchange it between assets, issue withdrawal links,
manage recurring subscriptions, and receive signed webhooks.

Human-readable documentation: https://docs.tgpaycrypto.com/crypto-pay-api-reference/

## Conventions

- **Authentication** — send your token in `TgPayCrypto-API-Token`.
  `TgCryptoPay-API-Token` and `Crypto-Pay-API-Token` are accepted aliases,
  in that order. The first non-empty header wins. Full-access primary
  tokens have every scope except `withdraw`; restricted tokens need the
  operation's scope, and only a restricted token can hold `withdraw`.
- **Envelope** — application success is HTTP 200 with `{ok: true, result}`;
  application errors are `{ok: false, error: {code, name}}`, with `code`
  equal to the HTTP status. Branch on `error.name`. Transport/framework
  rejections, such as malformed typed query parameters, may lack this envelope.
- **Amounts** — requests use decimal strings in whole-coin or fiat units,
  never JSON numbers. Crypto input is rounded to the asset's minor unit,
  with midpoint rounding away from zero; the result must be positive.
  Fiat input must represent a positive exact number of cents, at most
  10^13 whole fiat units. Responses use fixed-point strings; balance and
  fee amounts can be zero. `*_minor` values are integer strings.
  `getCurrencies` supplies asset decimals. Send exact asset precision.
- **POST parameters** — JSON object, form-urlencoded body, or URL query
  parameters; body values override query values, including null. Repeated
  form/query keys use the last value. Multipart is rejected. Money-moving
  methods have no GET aliases. Nested `items` and `recipients` must be
  JSON arrays in a JSON body; JSON-encoded strings do not work for them.
  Required fields must be present after merging query and body.
  Optional null values generally behave as omitted; per-field rules apply.
  Integers accept integer strings; booleans also accept 1/0 and the strings
  true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off (case-insensitive, surrounding whitespace ignored).
  Text limits are measured in UTF-16 code units by the server.
- **Idempotency** — `spend_id` is required for transfers, batch items,
  withdraw and exchange, optional for checks and refunds. Empty/null
  optional keys disable replay. Keys are scoped per app and operation;
  transfer, transferBatch and withdraw share a namespace, exchange has its
  own. After validation and access gates, the same parsed request
  replays its stored success. Different input returns `409 idempotency_conflict`;
  an unfinished claim returns `409 idempotency_in_progress`. Amount strings
  and recipient spelling are not normalized for the request hash: keep them
  identical on retries. Replays are snapshots, not refreshed objects; use
  list methods to obtain current status. createInvoice and plan creation
  have no spend_id idempotency; createInvoice's retry key is
  `client_invoice_id`.
- **Per-operation webhook and payload** — createInvoice, createCheck,
  transfer, each transferBatch item and withdraw accept `webhook_url`
  (a public HTTPS URL, up to 256 characters): every update of that
  operation goes there instead of the app's URL, regardless of the app's
  event selection. It is not returned in objects. createCheck, transfer,
  transferBatch items and withdraw also accept `payload` (up to 4096
  characters), echoed in the object and its webhooks.
- **Pagination** — invoices, checks, transfers, withdrawals, exchanges and
  withdrawal links default to offset 0, count 100; the server clamps
  offset to at least 0 and count to 1..1000.
  Subscriptions clamp count to 1..500. These lists return `{items: [...]}`,
  newest first. getSubscriptionPlans returns all plans without pagination.
- **Timestamps** — ISO-8601 strings; nullable timestamps are explicitly null.
- **Rate limits** — per app across its tokens, a counter per method:
  createInvoice/createCheck/editCheck/getInvoiceAddress/getExchangeEstimate
  60/min, refundInvoice/transfer/withdraw/exchange 30/min,
  transferBatch/updateApp 10/min, createSubscriptionPlan 20/min,
  createWithdrawalLink + deleteWithdrawalLink 60/min on one shared
  counter. Additional request limits may apply.
  On `429 rate_limited`, increase the delay before retrying.
- **Maintenance** — POST methods return `503 maintenance`; GET methods
  are not blocked by maintenance.

## Shared application errors

| HTTP | error.name | When |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | unauthorized | Missing/invalid/revoked/expired token, inactive app or blocked owner |
| 403 | scope_required | Token lacks the operation's scope |
| 400 | invalid_request | Invalid body, field type, length or numeric bounds |
| 429 | rate_limited | Request limit reached; increase the delay before retrying |
| 503 | maintenance | Maintenance blocks POST methods |
| 500 | internal_error | Unexpected server error |

transfer, transferBatch, createCheck, refundInvoice, withdraw and exchange
can also return `503 merchant_payouts_paused` or `403 verification_required`
when outgoing app funds are restricted. transfer, transferBatch and
createCheck enforce the owner's payout mode (`403 payouts_disabled` /
`recipient_not_allowed`); they and withdraw enforce the rolling daily
payout ceiling (`403 daily_cap_exceeded`). Refunds and exchanges do not
use those payout-mode/ceiling gates. getMe reports the mode and ceiling;
the owner changes them in the app, not through this API.

get.description:
Scope: none — any valid token.

Returns app identity, webhook settings, this token's scopes and label, and
read-only payout controls. scopes and token_name are null for the primary token.

Scope: `read`.

One row per enabled asset, including zero balances. available is spendable
app balance. onhold includes unclaimed check funds and pending username
transfers. deleteCheck refunds a check's unclaimed remainder; pending
transfers return to the app when processed for expiry. amount_minor is
available in minor units, not available plus onhold.

Scope: none — any valid token.

The authoritative list of crypto assets (`is_blockchain: true`) and
fiat currencies for pricing invoices (`is_fiat: true`), with per-currency
`decimals`. Treat this as the source of truth for what's live and
for amount math.

Scope: none — any valid token.

Returns indicative crypto-to-fiat quotes. is_valid=true does not guarantee
that a quote is current. If quotes are unavailable, the result may be an
empty array. Use the invoice's recorded amounts and rates to reconcile
an actual payment.

Scope: `read`.

Defaults to the last 24 hours. Naive datetimes are read as UTC; a
`Z` suffix is accepted.

Specific errors: `400 invalid_date` (unparsable `start_at`/`end_at`).

parameters.description: Window start (default now − 24 h).

parameters.name: end_at
parameters.description: Window end (default now).

post.description:
Scope: `invoices`. Rate limit: 60/min per app.

Crypto mode (default) fixes `asset`; fiat mode fixes `fiat` and the
payer picks one of `accepted_assets` at pay time. Invoices are paid
from the payer's TgPay Crypto wallet balance, or — when the owner has
turned on payment by a transfer to an address — by a transfer to the
invoice's own address (see getInvoiceAddress). Confirm the invoice is
`paid` before fulfilling the order. The platform fee comes out of the
merchant's share and is reported in `fee_amount`.

`client_invoice_id` makes creation retry-safe: a call repeating an id
already used by the app returns that existing invoice in its current
state (other parameters are not compared). `max_payments` > 1 makes
the invoice a reusable link: each payment becomes its own invoice with
`parent_invoice_id`, and the link counts `payments_count`.

Fiat invoices convert at the fresh pay-time rate rounded up in the
merchant's favor — unless an active `rate_lock_seconds` lock applies.
If no fresh rate is available, payment fails on the payer's side; the
merchant is never paid at a stale rate.

Specific errors:

| HTTP | `error.name` | when |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_currency` | missing asset in crypto mode; fiat mode without fiat or with non-empty asset; open_amount on a fiat invoice |
| 400 | `invalid_amount` | missing/unparsable/non-positive amount; `amount`+`open_amount` together; fiat amount not an exact number of cents or > 10^13 |
| 400 | `unknown_asset` | unknown/disabled `asset`, `swap_to`, or `accepted_assets` entry |
| 400 | `unsupported_fiat` | `fiat` not supported |
| 400 | `paid_btn_url_required` | `paid_btn_name` set without a valid http(s) `paid_btn_url` |
| 400 | `rate_lock_fiat_only` | positive `rate_lock_seconds` on a crypto-priced invoice |
| 409 | `ratelock_disabled` | rate-lock currently unavailable platform-side |
| 409 | `rate_unavailable` | no fresh rate for an accepted asset — retry |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | malformed parameters, including a `webhook_url` that is not a public HTTPS URL, a non-http(s) `success_url` / `cancel_url`, `success_url` together with `paid_btn_*`, an unknown or null key in `customer`, `max_payments` outside 1..1000000 |

Crypto mode ignores fiat and accepted_assets. A positive rate lock is
fiat-only; zero disables it. A lapsed lock reverts to fresh pay-time rates.
Creation has no spend_id replay protection. Optional payer-facing text
may be withheld on the payment screen while under review.

entries in invoice_ids are ignored; no valid ids means an empty list.

get.description:
Scope: `read`.

For reconciliation: every receipt of one invoice, oldest first — the
wallet payment (`method: balance`) and each transfer to an address
issued for the invoice (`method: address`). `paid` receipts at one
address add up to the amount quoted there, not to what arrived; a
transfer entirely above the quote is not listed.

Specific errors: `400 invalid_request` (missing or non-positive
`invoice_id`), `404 invoice_not_found`.

post.description:
Scope: `invoices`.

Cancels an **unpaid** invoice (active or expired). Result: `true`.

Specific errors: `404 invoice_not_found` (unknown id or another
app's invoice); `409 invoice_already_paid` (paid invoices can't be
deleted — money moved); `409 invoice_has_address` (an address was
issued for the invoice, and a transfer may still arrive there).

post.summary: The invoice's payment address in one network
post.description:
Scope: `invoices`. Rate limit: 60/min per app.

Returns the invoice's own payment address for the merchant's own
checkout, while payment by a transfer to an address is on for the
app. The payment window starts with the first call; a repeat call for
the same asset inside the window returns the same address, amount and
`expires_at` and never extends the window. An invoice has one address
per network; a call for another asset in the same network returns the
same address with a new amount, and only the latest amount and asset
count. A crypto invoice paid in its own asset uses its amount; any
other case is converted when the address is issued, rounded up.

Specific errors:

| HTTP | `error.name` | when |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | missing `invoice_id`, `asset` or `network` |
| 404 | `invoice_not_found` | unknown id / another app's invoice |
| 400 / 404 | `unknown_asset` / `unknown_network` | unknown asset or network |
| 409 | `checkout_disabled` | payment by address is off for the app |
| 409 | `invoice_already_paid` / `invoice_expired` | the invoice can no longer be paid |
| 400 | `asset_not_accepted` | the invoice can't be paid in this asset and network, or it is an open-amount invoice |
| 409 | `rate_unavailable` | no fresh rate to convert the amount — retry |
| 409 | `below_min_deposit` | the amount is under the network's minimum |
| 409 | `too_many_networks` | addresses are already issued in other networks |
| 409 | `checkout_busy` | too many of the app's invoices wait for a transfer — retry later |
| 503 | `checkout_unavailable` | no address can be issued in this network right now |

post.description:
Scope: `refunds`. Rate limit: 30/min
per app.

Returns a paid invoice's face amount — or part of it — from the app
balance to the payer, anonymous payers included, without revealing
them. The platform fee is not returned. Invoice `status` stays
`paid`; progress is tracked in the cumulative `refunded_amount` /
`refunded_minor`, and `refunded_at` is stamped once fully refunded.
Triggers the opt-in `refund_completed` webhook.

Specific errors:

| HTTP | `error.name` | when |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `invoice_not_found` | unknown id / another app's invoice |
| 400 | `invalid_amount` | unparsable or non-positive `amount` |
| 409 | `invoice_not_paid` | invoice isn't `paid` |
| 409 | `already_refunded` | nothing left to refund |
| 409 | `amount_too_big` | `amount` exceeds the unrefunded remainder |
| 409 | `insufficient_funds` | app balance can't cover the refund |
| 409 | `refund_unsupported` | the invoice was paid by a transfer to its address — there is no payer account |
| 409 | `idempotency_conflict` / `idempotency_in_progress` | see Conventions → Idempotency |

200.description: OK — the updated invoice with cumulative `refunded_*` fields.

post.description:
Scope: `checks`. Rate limit: 60/min per app. Shared payout restrictions apply.

Without recipients, creates a single-use check for amount. With recipients,
creates one claim per named recipient and funds the sum of their amounts;
top-level amount may be omitted, or is validated then ignored. Named lists
cannot be combined with a pin. Amounts are locked immediately and included
in getBalance.onhold. The unclaimed remainder returns on deletion or expiry.
The app owner cannot claim their own check. Password and expiry are optional.

Known recipient usernames bind to their user ids at creation; unknown
usernames remain claimable by the matching user when they join. Numeric
recipient ids need not already exist. A pin_to_username must resolve to an
existing available user; pin_to_user_id takes precedence over it.

check_activated fires on a single-use claim, or once per named seat with
activated_slot. check_expired fires only for expired named lists.
Optional non-empty spend_id enables stored-response replay.

`description` is shown on the check's page once it passes review (the
check is claimable either way) and can be changed later with editCheck;
`success_url` / `cancel_url` are Return buttons shown after a claim /
when the person can't claim. `payload` is echoed in the check object
and its webhooks; `webhook_url` receives this check's updates.

Specific errors: `400 unknown_asset`, `400 invalid_amount`,
`400 invalid_request` (including non-positive pin_to_user_id),
`400 invalid_recipient` (malformed named recipient or pin username),
`400 invalid_pinned_user` (named list combined with pin),
`400 invalid_slots` (more than 100 recipients), `400 self_claim`,
`400 duplicate_recipient`, `404 user_not_found` (unresolved/unavailable pin),
`400 amount_too_small` / `amount_too_big` (total outside payout USD bounds),
`409 insufficient_funds`, `409 idempotency_conflict` / `idempotency_in_progress`.

anyOf.description: Restrict claiming to this Telegram user ID.
Restrict by @username (leading @ optional, case-insensitive); ignored when pin_to_user_id is also given. Must belong to an existing user of the platform.
Optional replay key; empty/null disables idempotency.
Optional claim password; empty/null means no password. Never returned.
Seconds until expiry; zero, null or omitted means no explicit deadline. Choose a duration that produces a representable expiry timestamp.

Scope: `checks`. Rate limit: 60/min per app.

Sets, changes or removes the description of an active check the app
created; an empty or omitted `description` removes it. The new text is
reviewed as at creation. Nothing else about a check can be changed. No
money moves. Returns the updated check.

Specific errors: `400 invalid_request` (missing `check_id`, description
over 1024 characters), `404 check_not_found`, `409 check_not_active`
(fully claimed, expired or deleted).

post.summary: Pay out to a Telegram user
post.description:
Scope: `payouts`. Rate limit: 30/min per app. Shared payout restrictions apply.

Provide exactly one non-null recipient: user_id or username. A numeric id
must belong to an existing available user. A known username settles at once;
an unknown valid username creates a pending payout held in escrow. Forward
invite_url to the recipient. On claim it becomes completed; expiry processing
returns unclaimed funds to the app and sets returned. Read expires_at from
the response and track final status via getTransfers or opt-in terminal
webhooks. transfer sends to Telegram recipients; on-chain addresses use withdraw.

spend_id is required. Retrying replays the original response, even if a
pending payout has since completed. Platform amount limits are expressed
in USD; handle amount_too_small and amount_too_big. disable_send_notification suppresses only the immediate payout
notification; a later escrow claim still notifies the recipient.

Specific errors: `400 unknown_asset`, `400 invalid_request` (missing/both
recipients, non-positive user_id, invalid field type or length),
`400 invalid_recipient` (malformed username), `404 user_not_found` (unknown
numeric id or unavailable/blocked account), `400 invalid_amount`,
`400 amount_too_small` / `amount_too_big`, `409 insufficient_funds`,
`409 idempotency_conflict` / `idempotency_in_progress`.

post.description:
Scope: `payouts`. Rate limit: 10/min per app. Shared payout restrictions apply.

Submit 1..500 JSON items. The whole batch is parsed first: malformed rows
return `400 invalid_request`, repeated spend_id returns `400 duplicate_spend_id`.
The payout mode and daily ceiling can reject the whole batch with 403 before
any row executes. After those checks, items execute independently in order;
an application error on one row does not undo earlier rows. Each item uses
the same spend_id namespace as transfer. HTTP 200 / top-level ok=true may
include failed items: inspect every item's ok and error. Pending username
payouts are successful items even though they have not yet been claimed.
Per-item application errors match transfer. An unexpected server failure
can still abort the call after earlier rows committed; retry with the same
spend_ids and unchanged item parameters.

200.description: OK — one entry per input item, in order.

get.description:
Scope: `read`. Newest first. `spend_id` is an exact-match filter —
look up a payout by your own idempotency key.

Non-numeric transfer_ids entries are ignored; if no valid IDs remain, no rows are returned.
Only Telegram transfers are listed; on-chain payouts are listed by getWithdrawals.

post.summary: Withdraw the app balance to an external address
post.description:
Scope: `withdraw` — only a restricted token that holds it; the primary
token never has it (`403 scope_required`). Rate limit: 30/min per app.
Shared outgoing-funds restrictions and the daily payout ceiling apply;
the payout mode does not.

Available only when the owner has turned on withdrawals through the
API for the app (which requires a daily payout limit); otherwise
`403 withdraw_disabled`. Two optional owner safeguards: saved
addresses only (pass `address_id`, see getWithdrawAddresses) and an
IP allowlist (`403 ip_not_allowed`). The network fee is charged on top
of the amount from the app balance; the amount must reach the
network's minimum (getWithdrawFees). The owner's own withdrawal rules
apply too: withdrawal limits, address screening and the owner's
saved-addresses mode.

A new withdrawal returns `status: processing` with amount + fee on

replays the original response.

yet), `400 memo_unsupported`, `400 unknown_asset`, `404 unknown_network`,
`400 invalid_address`, `400 network_required`, `400 invalid_amount`,
`400 below_minimum`, `409 over_per_tx_limit` / `over_daily_limit`,
`409 over_unverified_daily_limit`, `409 insufficient_funds` (amount +
fee exceed the app balance), `403 address_not_allowlisted` /
`allowlist_pending`, `403 address_blocked` (screening),
`403 funds_under_review`, `403 pin_pending`, `403 daily_cap_exceeded`,
`503 withdrawals_paused` / `screening_unavailable` /
`withdraw_fee_unavailable` (retry later),

restrictions apply (`403 verification_required`,
`503 merchant_payouts_paused`); the payout mode and daily payout

Exchanges at the rate in effect at the call; there is no stored quote.
Pass exactly one of `amount` (give exactly this much `asset_from`;
guard with `min_amount_to`) or `amount_to` (receive exactly this much
`asset_to`; the spend is rounded up; guard with `max_amount_from`).
`spend_id` is required and has its own namespace. Each completed
exchange also sends the opt-in `exchange_completed` webhook.

Specific errors: `400 invalid_request` (missing parameter, both or
neither of `amount` / `amount_to`, a guard that doesn't match the
mode), `400 unknown_asset`, `400 invalid_amount`, `400 same_asset`,
`400 amount_too_small`, `400 exchange_min` / `exchange_max`,
`409 exchange_daily_limit`, `409 exchange_capacity`,
`409 exchange_disabled` / `exchange_asset_disabled`, `409 rate_moved`
(a guard was not met; nothing moved), `409 insufficient_funds`,
`503 rates_unavailable`, `403 exchange_unavailable` (exchange through
the API is switched off for the service),
`409 idempotency_conflict` / `idempotency_in_progress`.

Scope: `subscriptions`. Rate limit: 20/min per app.

The plan is an **immutable snapshot** — the mandate a user approves
is exactly this amount per this period; to change the price, create
a new plan and archive the old one. Users approve via the plan's
`mini_app_subscribe_url`; the first period is charged at approval.

`409 invalid_period` (below the platform minimum),
`409 too_many_plans` (active plan limit reached; archive one first).

Creation has no spend_id replay protection.

post.summary: An invoice was paid (delivered when a webhook URL is configured)
post.description:
invoice_paid is delivered when the app has a webhook URL. Other event
types require opt-in via updateApp.webhook_events or the app's settings.

Verify TgPayCrypto-API-Signature (identical aliases: TgCryptoPay-API-Signature
and Crypto-Pay-API-Signature): lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request
bytes, using as the HMAC key the raw SHA-256 digest of the app's signing
secret (whsec_..., created by the owner in the Mini App) when one is set,
otherwise of the app's current primary API token. Restricted tokens do not
sign webhooks. Without a signing secret, token rotation changes the signing
key; creating, replacing or removing the secret changes it too, in both
cases including for retries of queued deliveries.

A 2xx response received before the attempt times out acknowledges delivery.
Respond promptly and process long tasks separately. Failed deliveries are
retried with increasing delays, up to the platform's attempt limit. Delivery
is not guaranteed; use getInvoices to reconcile payments after an outage.
The webhook URL is not automatically disabled on failure. Retries keep update_id and the stored payload, while
request_date and the signature are regenerated per attempt. Deliveries use
the current configured URL and do not follow redirects. Dedupe by update_id.

Error.description:
Error — `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": <HTTP status>, "name":
"<machine_name>"}}` with the same HTTP status on the wire. See the
operation description for its specific error names and the API
description for the common ones.

Amount.description: Non-negative fixed-point decimal string in whole-coin (or fiat) units, including zero balances and fees. Never a JSON number.

AmountMinor.description: The integer minor-unit amount as a string (wei-scale values overflow the JS Number type).

name.description: Machine-readable error name to branch on, e.g. "insufficient_funds".

app_id.description: The app's public ID, serialized as a string.

payment_processing_bot_username.description: The Telegram bot whose Mini App processes payments.

webhook_events.description: Selected extended webhook update types. invoice_paid is automatic when a URL is configured and is not listed here.

scopes.description: This token's scopes, sorted; null = the primary token (every scope except withdraw).

token_name.description: The restricted token's label; null for the primary token.

daily_payout_max_usd_cents.description: Owner-set rolling 24-hour payout ceiling in USD cents; 0 means no ceiling.

daily_payout_spent_usd_cents.description: Spend currently counted toward the owner's rolling 24-hour payout limit, in USD cents. Includes transfers, checks and app withdrawals; invoice refunds are excluded.

payout_mode.description: off disables API payouts; allowlist permits only owner-listed recipients; any permits any valid recipient, including bearer checks.

onchain_pay_enabled.description: Whether buyers can pay this app's invoices by a transfer to the invoice's own address (see getInvoiceAddress). Read-only here: the owner switches it in the Mini App (Accepting payments). Off for a new app.

onhold.description: Funds held in unclaimed app checks and pending username transfers; not spendable.

decimals.description: Minor-unit exponent (crypto: per asset, up to 18; fiat: always 2).

is_valid.description: A true value does not guarantee that the quote is current.

rate.description: Fiat per 1 whole unit of source, as a fixed-point decimal string.

volume.description: USD value of invoices paid in the window, at current prices (best-effort).

conversion.description: Paid-in-window / created-in-window percentage, rounded to 2 decimal places; 0 when no invoices were created. May exceed 100 if older invoices are paid in the window.

unique_users_count.description: Distinct recorded payers of invoices paid in the window, including anonymous payments in this aggregate count.

anyOf.description: Required in crypto mode; non-empty asset is rejected in fiat mode.
Fiat mode: the fiat currency the invoice is priced in (is_fiat rows of getCurrencies).
Fiat mode: comma-separated asset codes or a JSON array. Omitted, null or empty list means all enabled assets.
Required unless open_amount. Crypto mode: in asset units; fiat mode: in fiat units, max 2 decimal places.
Crypto mode only: no fixed amount — the payer enters it at pay time. Mutually exclusive with amount.
Shown to the payer.
Shown to the payer only after payment.
Opaque merchant data echoed back in the invoice object and webhook.
Post-payment CTA button.
Required with paid_btn_name; must begin with lowercase http:// or https://. Without paid_btn_name it is ignored.
Auto-swap the received amount to this asset after payment, on a best-effort basis: if pricing, tradability or capacity is unavailable, the conversion is skipped and the paid asset is kept.
Seconds until expiry, at most 31 days. Omitted, null or zero uses the default lifetime. Read expiration_date in the response for the actual deadline; null means no deadline.
Fiat mode: positive value requests a rate lock, clamped to the platform window (minimum requested window 60 s). Zero/omitted/null disables the lock; expired locks revert to fresh rates.
A Return button after payment — the short form of the paid button (sets paid_btn_name to callback). Exclusive with paid_btn_name / paid_btn_url.
A Return button shown while the invoice is unpaid.
Form/query transport: the customer object as JSON text. An empty string means none.

How many payments one pay_url takes (default 1). Above 1, each payment becomes its own invoice with parent_invoice_id; the link itself is never paid and reads status paid once payments_count reaches max_payments. Such an invoice is paid from a wallet only, not by a transfer to an address.

period_no.description: Number of paid periods so far.

current_period_end.description: The paid-through deadline — read this as the access deadline.

SubscriptionCharge.description: The charge sub-object attached to subscription_charged webhook payloads.

update_id.description: Stable across redeliveries of the same event — dedupe on it.

request_date.description: Stamped per delivery attempt — UTC, ISO 8601 with microseconds (2026-08-11T12:00:00.123456Z).

payload.description: The full object for the event type.

UpdateAppRequest.description: Omitted or null fields leave their settings unchanged. An empty object is a no-op.

anyOf.description: Trimmed app name. Link/handle-shaped names and protected brand names are rejected.
Absolute public HTTPS URL, no embedded credentials; an empty string clears it. Redirects are not followed.

oneOf.description: Comma-separated list or JSON-encoded array of extended event names. An empty string clears the selection.

webhook_events.description: Replace the extended-event selection; [] clears it. invoice_paid is automatic when a URL is set and must not be included.

anyOf.description: Integer or integer string; parsed value must be within 1..9223372036854775807.
Optional leading @, case-insensitive; the normalized handle must start with a letter and contain 4..32 letters, digits or underscores.

AmountInput.description: Positive amount as a decimal string (not a JSON number). Surrounding whitespace and exponent notation are accepted. Crypto rounds to asset precision, midpoint away from zero, and must remain positive; fiat requires exact positive cents. Values must fit the server decimal parser and scaling arithmetic.

Withdrawal.description: The payout object — an on-chain withdrawal from the app balance (withdraw, getWithdrawals, and the kind=withdrawal variant of transfer webhooks). Same envelope shape as Transfer plus chain fields; distinguish it by kind=withdrawal.

transfer_id.description: Numeric withdrawal id; a separate id namespace from user transfers. Use kind and hash to distinguish.

fee_minor.description: The network fee charged on top of the amount, in minor units.

status.description: processing = held, delayed or broadcast; completed = confirmed on chain; failed = the hold (amount + fee) came back to the app balance.

txid.description: Null until the transaction is broadcast.

error.description: Failure detail when status=failed; null otherwise.

payload.description: Present only when the withdrawal was created with payload.

status.description: completed on transfer_completed; failed (not returned) on transfer_returned.

WithdrawalPayoutWebhook.description: Webhook-only on-chain payout variant of transfer_completed / transfer_returned, made through withdraw or the app's Payouts screen. transfer/transferBatch cannot create it and getTransfers does not list it (getWithdrawals does). Distinguish it by kind=withdrawal.

PositiveIdInput.description: Integer or integer string; parsed value must be within 1..9223372036854775807.

OperationWebhookUrl.description: This operation's own webhook address — an absolute public HTTPS URL, no embedded credentials, surrounding spaces trimmed. Every update of the operation goes here instead of the app's webhook URL, regardless of the app's event selection. An empty string means the app's URL. Not returned in objects. With a spend_id it is part of the compared request.

OperationPayload.description: Your own data, echoed in the object and its webhooks. An empty string means none.

ReturnUrl.description: An absolute http:// or https:// URL; surrounding spaces trimmed, an empty string means none.

CustomerInput.description: The seller's own record of the buyer, echoed in the invoice and its webhooks; the payer does not see it. Only these four keys; each value is a scalar whose text form is 1–256 characters (null values are rejected). An empty object means none.

method.description: balance = paid from a TgPay Crypto wallet; address = a transfer to the invoice's address.

status.description: paid = paid the invoice; pending = credited at the address, the invoice is still short; late = came too late and was credited to the app balance minus fee_amount; review = held for a manual check, does not pay the invoice meanwhile.

amount.description: The amount counted for this receipt — a paid transfer is cut at what was still owed.

fee_amount.description: The fee kept from a late receipt; null otherwise (a paid invoice's fee is the invoice's fee_amount).

usd_amount.description: USD value of the transfer at arrival; null for balance and when amount is only part of the transfer.

from_address.description: The sender's address — it can belong to an exchange rather than the buyer.

paid_by_user_id.description: The payer's Telegram ID on a balance receipt; null when anonymous and on every address receipt.

items.description: Oldest first; empty when nothing arrived.

InvoiceLatePayment.description: The late transfer credited to the app balance (invoice_late_payment).

fee_amount.description: The fee kept from it, in the same asset; the rest is on the app balance.

asset.description: The asset the payer sends (case-insensitive). A crypto invoice accepts its own asset and other supported assets; a fiat invoice its accepted_assets; the owner's list narrows both.

network.description: The network code of that asset (case-insensitive).

status.description: The payment at this address. waiting = nothing yet; confirming = seen on the network, waiting for confirmations; underpaid = part arrived, the rest goes to the same address; review = held for a manual check; late = came too late, credited to the app balance; expired = the window ended unpaid.

memo.description: Show it with the address in networks that use one.

amount.description: The exact amount to send, in asset.

received.description: Credited at this address so far.

seen.description: Found in a block but not yet confirmed.

expires_at.description: The end of the payment window.

pay_page_url.description: The invoice's ready-made public payment page.

anyOf.description: The new description; an empty string removes it.

amount.description: The amount to deliver; the network fee is charged on top from the app balance.

spend_id.description: Required idempotency key, shared with transfer.

anyOf.description: A saved address (getWithdrawAddresses); required under saved-addresses-only. Exactly one of address_id / address.
The destination address. Exactly one of address_id / address.
Network code; needed when the address is valid on several of the asset's networks. A saved address uses its own network.
Memo / tag for address; only networks that support one. Not allowed with address_id.
Your note, returned in the object and webhooks; not sent to the blockchain.

fee.description: The network fee charged on top of the amount.

fee_empty.description: The fee to an address that was never used, on networks that charge more for it; null elsewhere.

min_amount.description: The smallest amount that can be withdrawn.

address_id.description: The id to pass to withdraw.

label.description: The owner's name for the address; can be empty.

usable_at.description: When the address can first be used.

usable.description: False before usable_at — a withdrawal to it returns 409 address_pending.

UsdAmount.description: USD as a decimal string with two decimal places.

assets.description: Any two different assets of the list form a pair.

daily_max_usd.description: The app's rolling 24-hour limit; "0.00" = no limit.

rate.description: asset_to per one unit of asset_from, margin included.

anyOf.description: Give exactly this much asset_from. Exactly one of amount / amount_to.
Receive exactly this much asset_to; the spend is rounded up. Exactly one of amount / amount_to.

spend_id.description: Required idempotency key; exchanges have their own namespace.

anyOf.description: With amount only — the least asset_to accepted, else 409 rate_moved.
With amount_to only — the most asset_from to give, else 409 rate_moved.

Exchange.description: The exchange object — exchange, getExchanges and the exchange_completed webhook.

rate.description: asset_to per one unit of asset_from, margin included.

anyOf.description: Network code; needed when the address is valid on several of the asset's networks.
Omitted = the person enters the amount.
Memo / tag for address; only networks that support one.
Seconds the link works, 60..2592000 (30 days); default 86400.

mini_app_withdrawal_url.description: The t.me link to give the person.

network.description: Filled in even when not passed.

amount.description: Decimal string, or null when the person enters the amount.
